record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run. The README says probe and steering results are pending unless the activation run finished, and reports no such results.
record.tranche_reason: The repo reports refusal changes under benchmark versus user framing, but does not test the difference-in-means refusal direction or any of V1–V8. Its implemented probe and steering concern an eval-versus-user direction, and their results are pending.
record.gate_note: The refusal-format results below bear on refusal behavior but not on any listed version, so they are recorded with versions ["none"]. Excluded eval-versus-user classification and verbalised-awareness results because they do not measure refusal or the claimed refusal direction. Probe and steering scripts are described as implemented, not as having reported results.
record.test_reason: The repository measures how benchmark versus user framing changes refusal rates. It never computes, ablates, adds or edits the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. Its only direction is an eval-versus-user steering vector, and those results are pending. It does not cite the original paper, so 'discusses' is a loose fit: the work is adjacent, not engaged with the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. It should add the authors' takeaway that refusal benchmarks in scaffolded formats overstate compliance with real users. It should also add that the shift occurs with almost no verbalised evaluation awareness (≤2.4%), which matters for monitoring. The probe and steering results are pending.
record.recipe_differences: Not a replication of the refusal-direction method; this GitHub repository is an evaluation project with an implemented probe and steering test for an eval-versus-user direction, but those results are pending.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal changes with benchmark format: numbered/rubric increases refusal, while MCQ, scenario, and harness formats decrease it for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. Qwen's refusal shift also differs by request category.

fits_no_version.finding: With the request text held fixed, benchmark-style scaffolding changes refusal rates in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. It is −13.9 pp overall. The sign depends on format: rubric gives +5.2, while scenario, harness and MCQ give −16 to −24. Benign requests show no shift. Gemini Flash-Lite models barely move.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Surface benchmark formatting, with the request held fixed, can shift refusal rates in small open models, in a format-dependent direction.

record.problems: Refusal labels use a classifier plus an MCQ rule, and the README reports imperfect agreement with the judge; it says the full-set magnitude is likely overstated by the scorer. Templates are overt and less naturalistic than real prompts. Gemini samples are small and have wide intervals; Qwen covers 1,680 of 2,219 pairs. No general-capability test is reported. Probe and steering results are pending. The README reports 168 judged responses in one place and refers to a 180-response sample in its limitations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional refusal-direction rows: the README says the probe and steering runs are pending, so scripts and planned analyses do not establish results. Excluded eval-style classification and verbalised-awareness outcomes because they do not measure refusal or the claimed refusal direction.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction, ablation, addition or capability check.
Format effects on refusal are shown, but there is no test of whether they act by suppressing the refusal direction, and no adversarial training.
No separation of harmfulness representation from the refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer.
No reasoning models tested; Gemini was run with minimal thinking and gives behavioural results only.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no version is tested. The planned steering, h + α(μ_eval − μ_user) on refusal, would be a difference-in-means intervention on refusal, but along an eval-awareness direction rather than the refusal direction. No results were reported, so it bears on no version. The README is inconsistent about the size of the judged sample (168 vs 180 responses).

versions.untested_parts: No test of the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, its ablation, addition, or effects on other abilities.
No weight edit or abliteration result.
No test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No test of how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
